title: Alibaba Group Holding Ltd (NYSE:BABA) and Foxconn Led a $348 million funding into Xiaopeng Motors
text:
January 29, 2018 Alibaba Group Holding Ltd (NYSE:BABA) and Foxconn Led a $348 million funding into Xiaopeng Motors 
Foxconn Technology Group and Chinese e-commerce giant Alibaba Group Holding Ltd (NYSE:BABA) have co-led a $348 million funding into Xiaopeng Motors, a Chinese electric-vehicle manufacturer, to tap electronic car’s through its investment, which marks as Alibaba (BABA)’s first ever and big investment in a car maker. 
There is also a Venture capital firm IDG Capital, which was the third lead investor in the funding, and in the car maker industry, the funds are slated for both the research and production costs, Xiaopeng said in a release Monday. 
The executives of both companies said that in the release that Xpeng gives the company the ability to tap into the intersection of artificial intelligence, the internet, and traditional manufacturing, definitely a viable area with a lot of promise. Foxconn, which is formally Hon Hai Precision is based in Taiwan, and is best reknowned for manufacturing Apple Inc.’s (AAPL) iPhones. 
Chinese companies are investing in car industry a lot, as two other Chinese internet giants, Baidu Inc (ADR) (NASDAQ:BIDU),and Tencent Holdings, both have led funding’s of at least $2.5 billion into Chinese electric-car companies, which includes WM Motor Technology and NiO. Tencent has also invested $1.8 billion for a 5 percent stake in Tesla Motors Inc (NASDAQ:TSLA) in last March.
